key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr provided the lowest measured wear rate and best corrosion resistance, while HVOF achieved the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: HVAF is a promising coating route for 304 stainless steel components requiring combined wear and corrosion protection.
method: Deposit WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation, HVOF and HVAF spraying.
Compare coating microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction, wear and corrosion behavior.
Examine wear tracks to identify abrasive and fatigue wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: HVAF reduced wear rate from (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ to (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m) versus uncoated steel and achieved the lowest coating corrosion current density, (1.75±0.02) µA/cm².
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test environments or spray parameters, limiting direct transfer of the performance ranking to service conditions.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
